concepts.name: Meaning and definitions of a constitution

questions.q: The term 'constitution' is derived from the Latin word 'constituere'. In the present sense, the term refers to
questions.a: a set of principles on the organisation and working of government and on its relationship with the people in terms of rights and duties
o: a set of principles on the organisation and working of government and on its relationship with the people in terms of rights and duties
a set of principles that fix the fundamental rights of the citizens against the State, without dealing with how the government is organised or works
a body of ordinary laws made by the legislature to regulate the trade and taxation of the State and the conduct of its officials
a code of customs that binds the rulers but does not specify the organs of government or the rights and duties of the people
questions.e: Constituere means 'to establish' or 'to set-up'; the present sense is a set of principles on the organisation and working of government and its relationship with the people in terms of rights and duties.
w: It leaves out how the government is organised and works, which the definition includes.
The chapter describes principles on government and on rights and duties, not ordinary trade and tax laws.
The definition covers the organs of government and the people's rights and duties; it is not a mere code of customs.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the descriptions commonly used for a constitution?
questions.e: A constitution is described as the fundamental law of the land, supreme law of the state, basic law of the country, instrument of the government, rules of the state, basic structure of the polity and grundnorm of the country. 'Charter of the judiciary' is not one of these descriptions.
w: It is used: the constitution is described as the 'grundnorm of the country' (Kelsen's term for the basic norm).
It is used: the constitution is described as the 'instrument of the government'.
It is used: the constitution is described as the 'basic structure of the polity'.

questions.e: The 'fundamental principles that determine the form of a state' definition is Gettell's.
w: Gilchrist speaks of a body of rules or laws determining the organisation of government and the distribution of powers.
Wheare speaks of the whole system of government and the collection of rules which govern the government.
Wade and Phillips speak of a document having a special legal sanctity.

w: It covers organisation of government, distribution of powers and the principles of exercising them; the people are not mentioned.
It speaks of the whole system of government and the rules which govern the government, not the relation to the people.
It covers the framework and functions of organs and the principles of their operation, not the relation to the people.

questions.e: Gilchrist names the organization of government, the distribution of powers and the general principles on which powers are exercised. 'The scope and manner of exercise of governmental functions' belongs to Gettell's definition.
